title: Four-legged knot stitch
subtitle: A scattered filling of upright crosses locked at the centre with a knot
excerpt: Four-legged knot stitch places individual crossed units across a shape, each one made from a vertical bar and a horizontal bar joined at the centre by a firm knot. The knot is formed by passing the thread under both bars at the intersection before the horizontal arm is completed. The result is a light, even filling with a textured dot at each unit centre.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopaedia of Needlework (1886), knotted stitches chapter (Project Gutenberg #20776). Caulfeild and Saward, Dictionary of Needlework (1882), four-legged knot stitch entry.

content.text: Four-legged knot stitch builds a scattered filling from individual cross units. Each unit has four arms, two vertical and two horizontal, meeting at a central knot. The knot is made by passing the needle under both bars at the intersection and looping the thread around the needle before pulling through. The bars do not cross diagonally, they sit upright like a plus sign, and the knot locks the centre without piercing the fabric a second time at that point.

items.label: Thread
items.value: Stranded cotton 2 to 3 strands, or perle 8 for a firmer knot

content.text: Secure the thread on the back and bring it up at (A), the top of the unit. Insert the needle at (B), directly below (A), to lay a vertical bar. Bring the needle up at (C), to the left of the bar at mid-height, but do not pull fully through yet.
Before pulling through at (C), slide the needle under the vertical bar from left to right, without piercing the fabric. The needle tip passes between the bar and the fabric surface.

Loop the working thread under the needle tip, from right to left, to form the knot. Hold the loop in place with a thumb while you pull the needle through. The thread tightens around both bars at the centre, forming the locking knot.
Insert the needle at (D), directly to the right of centre at the same height as (C), to complete the horizontal arm. Pull through to the back. The unit is now finished.
Bring the thread up at the top of the next unit position and repeat. Space units evenly across the area being filled.

attrs.heading: When four-legged knot stitch goes wrong

items.symptom: The knot is missing and the bars just cross loosely
items.cause: The thread was not looped under the needle tip before pulling through at the centre.
items.fix: After sliding the needle under the vertical bar, stop and check the working thread is looped beneath the needle. Only then pull through. The knot should tighten visibly at the intersection.

items.symptom: The horizontal arm pulls the knot off-centre
items.cause: The needle is inserted at (D) before the knot has fully tightened.
items.fix: Let the knot settle first. Ease the thread gently until the knot sits firm at the crossing point, then take the needle down at (D).
